title: ENDEX: Red Flag Expires, Coyote Draw Fire at 2,900 Acres

fields.resolution: ENDEX — EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE. It is 20:30 MDT on Wednesday 14 April 2027, and the Red Flag Warning expired at 20:00. Gulch Saddle reads west 19 mph, gusting 38 mph, with humidity up to 16 percent, and the Incident Commander reports the Coyote Draw Fire at about 2,900 acres with 5 percent containment. The head has slowed at the west edge of Gulch Village, and no structures in Kestrel Springs have burned. This ends play; hold your pens.
finalState: NWS fire weather desk: gusts expected to stay below 35 mph from late tonight. The Kestrel Springs pump station was refueled under escort, and hydrant supply is holding.
The PG-01 segment of Circuit 11 has stayed de-energized since Crew 11-B reopened the sectionalizer. Circuits 6, 7, 11 and 12 stay dead overnight.

Phased restoration starts at first light Thursday 15 April after a full daylight patrol (4 to 8 hours) and 2 hours of gusts below 35 mph. Well 2, the Pine Gulch Medical Center feed and medical baseline households go first.

Any circuit segment in a zone under Evacuation Warning or Evacuation Order stays de-energized until the county declares the zone repopulated, after a joint Sheriff and fire decision on the criteria the EOC recorded tonight.
The zone board, the 17:00 and later shared road status lists, and the decision log are frozen as they stand for review.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Stop all play now. Leave your logs, the zone board, the road status list and your decision records exactly as they are; don't fix anything. Take ten minutes, then bring your notes back to the main table for the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: Timeline walk-back, then 3-Up, 3-Down: we rebuild the day on the board from the 06:00 shutoff decision through the 15:10 order time for PG-03 and the 17:38 PG-01 re-energization. Then each role names three things that worked and three that broke.
hotWashQuestions: Battalion 1 put the latest order time for PG-03 at 15:10. When did the order actually go out, how did that compare with projected arrival minus the 55-minute clearance, and what slowed the decision?
How did the shutoff decision and the zone statuses stay linked, or come apart? Why did Crew 11-B have a 13:00 list showing PG-01 with no status, and who owns getting zone status to the co-op?
Acreage of 1,200, 1,500, 3,000 and 2,300 was all in public view. Who confirmed the zone status and acreage before release, and did the Sheriff, fire, co-op, schools and hospital use the same words?
With PG-14 and the Kestrel Ridge site down and 153 SawmillAlert calls failing, how did we reach KS-04, Stonebridge and the unconfirmed medical baseline household on Gulch Road?
What repopulation and re-energization criteria did the EOC record tonight, and who signs off on each before a single customer in a Warning or Order zone gets power back?
fields.facilitatorNote: Photograph the zone board, the shared road status list and the decision log before anyone touches them. Collect every role's log and the evaluator sheets before the break. Pull the actual PG-03 order time for the timeline walk-back.
fields.scenarioTitle: One Road Out — PSPS, Evacuation Timing & Shared Zone Status

instructorNote: Ends play and moves the room into the hot wash. Make sure all players stop, leave their logs, zone board and decision records as they stand, and go into a review of evacuation timing, the link between shutoff and zone status, and message consistency.
